'''Aleksandr Dmitriyevich Garnovskii''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Дмитриевич Гарновский}}; 30 August 1932 in [[Rostov-on-Don]] – 9 December 2010 in [[Rostov-on-Don]]) was a [[Russians|Russian]] [[chemist]]. [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Chemical Sciences]], [[Professor]].

== Biography ==
Aleksandr Dmitriyevich Garnovskii graduated from the Chemical Faculty of [[Rostov State University]] in 1956. In 1961—1979 he also worked there; since 1974 he was a Professor of the Department of Physical and Colloid Chemistry of the RSU. In 1979—1983 he was the head of the Department of Chemistry of Rostov Institute of Agricultural Engineering (now [[Don State Technical University]]). Since 1983 he was the head of the Department of Chemistry of Coordination Compounds of the Research Institute of Physical and Organic Chemistry of the RSU.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ipoc.sfedu.ru/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=66|title=IPOC - Гарновский Александр Дмитриевич|website=www.ipoc.sfedu.ru|access-date=2018-05-16|archive-date=2014-10-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141011204144/http://www.ipoc.sfedu.ru/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=66|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Garnovskii was a specialist in the field of chemistry of heterocyclic and coordination compounds. He developed original techniques for the production of a number of [[azomethine]] and [[azole]] compounds, stereo- and regioselective synthesis of their complexes with various metals. He formulated the rules of nucleophilic and electrophilic substitution in a series of imidazole derivatives; he also formulated and substantiated the laws of competitive coordination of ambiguous chelating ligands. He carried out a series of studies on tribochemical synthesis of coordination compounds.<ref name=":0" />

Garnovskii was a member of the editorial board of the ''Journal of Coordination Chemistry''. He was the author of more than 800 scientific works, 11 [[monographs]]. He had 30 copyright certificates of the USSR and 3 patents of the Russian Federation.<ref name=":0" /> Today he is one of the most cited chemists in Russia.<ref>[http://www.scientific.ru/whoiswho/active8.html Scientific.ru]</ref>

He was a laureate of the [[State Prize of the USSR]] (1989)<ref name=":0" /> and [[Lev Chugaev]] Prize ([[Russian Academy of Sciences]], 2003),<ref>[http://www.ras.ru/win/db/award_dsc.asp?P=id-102.ln-ru Премия имени Л. А. Чугаева — Список награждённых]</ref> and Honoured Scientist of the Russian Federation (1997), an Honorary Worker of Higher Professional Education of the Russian Federation (2002) and a Member of Russian Academy of Natural Sciences (1992).<ref name=":0" />

* A.D.Garnovskii, B.I.Kharisov, V.V.Skopenko, L.M.Blanco, N.N.Kokozay, A.S.Kuzharov, D.A.Garnovskii, O.Yu.Vassilyeva, A.S.Burlov, V.A.Pavlenko. Direct Synthesis of Coordination and Organometallic Compounds (A.D.Garnovskii and B.I.Kharisov, Eds.). — Elsevier, Amsterdam, 1999.
